messages:
Linda (Support): Hey team — Acme reports the dashboard shows a 15,000 credit visible at the org and project banner, but their API usage/ledger shows no credit offsets. Theyre stuck on a staging deploy.
Sam (BillingEng): Can you share org_id and a sample service key so I can look up grants and allocations?
Linda (Support): org_id: org-acme-8f4, project: acme-staging, example key (redacted): sk-live-abc123
Olivia (Backend): Repro steps provided by customer:
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc123" https://api.redwood.com/v1/usage?project=acme-staging
2) GET https://api.redwood.com/v1/billing/ledger?project=acme-staging
Observed: usage shows tokens consumed, ledger shows charge lines, no credit line or allocation present.
Michael (SRE): Any audit event when the credit was created? UI can show org-wide banners even if grant wasnt allocated to projects/service keys.
Linda (Support): Pulled audit snippet from internal audit stream:
```
2026-02-25T20:07:12Z grant.create id=grant-9134 type=promo amount=15000 scope=org org_id=org-acme-8f4 apply_to_projects=false created_by=partner-portal partner_id=partner-998
```
Tara (Product): That explains it: apply_to_projects=false. Partner portal flow created an org-scoped grant but did not allocate to projects automatically. The UI surfaces org banners for visibility, which led to confusion. We should improve the partner UX to call this out.
Sam (BillingEng): For billing, org-scoped grants need explicit grant_allocations entries per project/servicekey to produce ledger credit lines. We have a one-off allocation tool: `scripts/alloc_org_grants_to_projects.py --org org-acme-8f4`. But we should run checks before allocating.
Olivia (Backend): Quick check results:
```
SELECT id FROM grant_allocations WHERE grant_id = 'grant-9134';
-- no rows
```
So no allocations exist yet.
Michael (SRE): Plan: run a dry-run allocation, preview ledger, then perform allocation with audit tags. Steps:
- dry-run: `ALLOCATE_GRANT --grant grant-9134 --org org-acme-8f4 --dry-run`
- preview: GET /internal/billing/preview?grant=grant-9134
- allocate: `ALLOCATE_GRANT --grant grant-9134 --org org-acme-8f4 --metadata "support:manual-alloc"`
Sam (BillingEng): Please include partner_id in allocation metadata and set reason "support: manual allocate per customer request". Also ensure we do not apply credits to past closed invoices; allocation should only affect open metering windows.
Linda (Support): Customer is asking for ETA; they need credits applied by EOD PST.
Tara (Product): I'll open a tiny UX ticket to make apply_to_projects explicit in partner portal: https://git.redwood.com/r/redwood/product/PR-1224 (brief PR, adds tooltip).
redwood-bot: support-ticket #462111 created for org-acme-8f4 (https://support.redwood.com/t/462111). Assigned to Linda + Sam.
Sam (BillingEng): I'll run the allocation at 17:10 PST and report back.
Olivia (Backend): After allocation we expect ledger lines like:
```
2026-02-25T17:12:01Z ledger.credit grant=grant-9134 project=acme-staging amount=15000 note="support:manual-alloc partner=partner-998"
```
Michael (SRE): Post-run checklist:
- confirm GET /v1/billing/ledger?project=acme-staging returns credit lines
- confirm GET /v1/usage reflects net charges or credit balance
- write audit entry for allocation operation
Sam (BillingEng): allocation complete ✅
Olivia (Backend): Verified ledger now shows credit 15000 applied to acme-staging; usage queries reflect reduced net charges.
Linda (Support): Customer confirmed they see credit in both UI and API billing now, and staging deploy can proceed. Marking ticket resolved after follow-up email.
Tara (Product): Filed partner portal UX tweak; follow-up to add clearer language around org-scoped grants and an optional auto-allocate checkbox.
Linda (Support): thanks everyone, closing loop. :thumbsup:
